title: Benchmark lineage anchoring & judge-ensemble calibration playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: define a repeatable playbook for how we create and evolve benchmark baselines (lineage), calibrate LLM-as-judge ensembles, and gate config/model rollouts. Motivation: recent rollouts exposed brittleness when benchmark anchors drifted with upstream data and when single-judge decisions produced noisy pass/fail signals. This initiative produces actionable rules: how to add or retire anchors, how to weight judges in an ensemble, statistical thresholds for gating, and how to surface human spot-checks for edge cases.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical benchmark lineage metadata is captured for each release candidate (model/config hash, dataset snapshot id, cohort definitions)
A judge-ensemble config schema exists that allows weighting per-judge and per-cohort, and is persisted with eval runs
Calibration routine implemented that outputs confidence intervals for delta scores and recommends gating decisions (pass/canary/block)
Automatic canary gating rules enforce rollback when negative delta exceeds calibrated threshold with p-value < 0.05 for high-impact cohorts
Runbook documented with human spot-check sampling policy and Slack/Console alert templates
notes: Scope excludes upstream data labeling changes — that will be handled by a separate labeling governance effort
We will reuse existing eval infra (evals-runner + judge infra) but extend job payload with lineage metadata and ensemble weights
Plan to pilot on two products: Chat Replies and Retrieval-Rerank cohorts to validate cross-workload behavior

decision_log: Adopt judge-ensemble with tiered anchors (primary/secondary/synthetic) - reduces single-judge noise
Use bootstrapped CI + multiple-hypothesis correction for cohort-level gating
Human spot-checking required for any auto-block triggered by secondary-cohort signals
risks: Storage cost increase from retaining dataset snapshots - mitigated by retention policy
Overfitting to current anchor set; mitigated by quarterly anchor review and synthetic anchor generation
Increased time-to-detect rare regressions due to higher statistical thresholds
